title: Entity System
lead: Auto-detecting and disambiguating the people, projects, and systems in your text.
summary: MemPalace's entity system detects and classifies proper nouns (people, projects, topics) from content using a two-pass signal-based approach: extraction via i18n-aware regex with COCA content-word filtering, then scoring via contextual signals (dialogue markers, pronouns, action verbs, versioning). A persistent EntityRegistry seeds from onboarding, learns high-confidence candidates, and researches unknowns via Wikipedia. Corpus-origin detection separates AI-dialogue agent personas from real people before classification. Entities key wings and feed hallway computation.

concepts.definition: Tier 2 linguistics cleanup: a frozenset of ~600 common English words (code, phase, brutal, line, note) that appear capitalized but are not proper nouns. Blocks false-positive entity detection on sentence-start words. Multi-word candidates intentionally bypass this filter to preserve compounds like 'Claude Code'.

A person must exhibit signals from TWO different categories (dialogue, action, pronoun, direct-address) to confidently classify. Single-category hits (e.g., only action verbs) are downgraded to 'uncertain' to prevent false positives from syntactic patterns like 'Click, click, click...' being mistaken for person-entity 'Click'.

Two-tier system (Tier 1 heuristic + optional Tier 2 LLM) that determines whether a corpus is AI-dialogue vs narrative. Tier 1 uses brand-term regex (unambiguous: 'Claude Code', ambiguous: 'Claude') with co-occurrence rules. Tier 2 (LLM-optional) extracts platform identity and agent-persona names. Persona-matched candidates are reclassified from people->agent_personas to prevent false positive family/relationship inference.

Locales with combining-mark scripts (Devanagari, Arabic, Thai, Khmer) declare boundary_chars in i18n entity sections. These expand Python's default \b to a lookaround-based boundary that preserves marks, so names like अनीता match correctly instead of truncating to अनीत.

Persistent ~/.mempalace/entity_registry.json storing three tiers: (1) onboarding (user explicitly confirmed), (2) learned (high-confidence detections from sessions), (3) wiki (researched via Wikipedia API, local-only by default for privacy). Supports ambiguous-flag disambiguation, alias tracking, and relationship metadata.

Extracted proper nouns embedded in closet lines as the 2nd pipe-separated field. Detected via i18n-aware patterns on a content window. Entities appearing 2+ times in the window are extracted (max 5), deduped, ranked by frequency. Feeds palace-level searching and hallway computation.

Names the user has assigned to AI agents they converse with (e.g., Echo, Sparrow, Claude-instance-2). Extracted by Tier 2 (LLM) during corpus-origin detection. When corpus_origin context is passed to detect_entities, candidates matching agent-persona names are reclassified from people/uncertain into a separate agent_personas bucket.

For ambiguous words (ever, grace, may, Rose) that are also common English words, EntityRegistry._disambiguate() checks surrounding context against person-context patterns (said, with, 's) and concept-context patterns (have you, if you, would). Context-derived confidence adjusts the classification decision.

symbols.name: extract_candidates
symbols.role: Pass 1: extracts capitalized proper noun candidates from text via i18n regex patterns, COCA filter, stopwords; returns {name: frequency >= 3}

symbols.name: score_entity
symbols.role: Pass 2: scores a candidate across six signal types (dialogue, pronouns, verbs, direct address, versioning, code refs); returns {person_score, project_score, signals}

symbols.name: classify_entity
symbols.role: Applies two-signal-category rule and confidence calibration to classify candidate as person/project/uncertain

symbols.name: detect_entities
symbols.role: Main entry point: scans files, extracts candidates, scores/classifies each, applies optional corpus_origin persona reclassification; returns {people, projects, uncertain, [agent_personas]}

symbols.name: confirm_entities
symbols.role: Interactive review: user edits detected entities, adds missing ones, returns confirmed {people, projects, topics}

symbols.name: EntityRegistry
symbols.role: Persistent registry at ~/.mempalace/entity_registry.json; three-tier lookup (onboarding > learned > wiki); supports disambiguation, Wikipedia research (network-optional), atomic writes

symbols.name: _get_coca_filter
symbols.role: Lazy-loads frozenset of ~600 common English content words from data/coca_content_words.json; O(1) cache hit via lru_cache

symbols.name: detect_origin_heuristic
symbols.role: Tier 1: grep-based AI-dialogue detection; counts unambiguous/ambiguous brand terms and turn-markers with co-occurrence rule; cheap, no API

symbols.name: detect_origin_llm
symbols.role: Tier 2: LLM-assisted; extracts primary_platform, user_name, agent_persona_names; falls back conservatively on any error

symbols.name: _apply_corpus_origin
symbols.role: Reclassifies candidates matching agent_persona_names into agent_personas bucket; prevents AI instances populating family/relationship drawers

symbols.name: build_closet_lines
symbols.role: Mines drawer content: extracts entities via i18n patterns, dedupes on count >= 2, COCA-filters, embeds in closet lines as pipe-separated entities field

symbols.name: _candidate_entity_words
symbols.role: Finds capitalized candidates via i18n-aware patterns; same logic as entity_detector.extract_candidates; used by closets and hallways

surprises.title: Multi-Word Candidates Bypass COCA Filter
surprises.detail: Single-word candidates apply the COCA content-word filter to suppress 'Code', 'Phase', 'Note', etc. But multi-word candidates are intentionally NOT filtered. This preserves compound names like 'Claude Code' (where 'Code' alone would be suppressed). A deliberate design decision favoring recall over precision.

surprises.title: Two-Signal-Category Enforcement Against Syntactic Artifacts
surprises.detail: A word like 'Click' appearing 15 times can match the person-verb pattern repeatedly, accumulating high person_score from a single signal category. The two-signal-category rule prevents this from classifying Click as a person unless it also exhibits dialogue markers, pronouns, or direct address.

surprises.title: Ambiguous-Term Co-Occurrence Rules Out Literal False Positives
surprises.detail: A French novel with character 'Claude', astrology corpus full of 'Gemini', or poetry about 'haiku' could false-positive as AI-dialogue. The co-occurrence rule (ambiguous terms only count if unambiguous term or turn-marker present) solves this, preventing real family members from being marked as AI personas.

surprises.title: Pronoun-Only Classification Requires High Ratio
surprises.detail: A diary protagonist mentioned 100 times, referenced with pronouns 20 times, scores person via pronoun signal alone only if pronoun_hits >= 5 AND pronoun_hits / frequency >= 0.2. This 20% ratio threshold prevents common sentence-start words that incidentally appear near pronouns from qualifying.

surprises.title: Closet Entity Dedup Happens Pre-Sort, Pre-Cap
surprises.detail: Entity dedup in closet lines uses word_freq dict counting, a single-pass O(n) dedup. Only after counting do we filter (>= 2), sort by frequency, cap at 5. Efficient but relies on correct word-boundary extraction to avoid double-counting 'Max' and 'max'.

designDecisions.rationale: Onboarding (confidence 1.0) seeds ground truth the user explicitly confirmed. Learned entities (auto-added from sessions) require high confidence (>0.75) to avoid proliferation. Wiki is research-only, network-gated, never auto-added. The ordering honors user intent first, then high-confidence inference, then optional external research, matching the local-first, zero-API philosophy.

Determines platform and agent-persona names before detect_entities runs, preventing catastrophic downstream errors: an AI instance 'Echo' shouldn't populate family/relationship drawers. Tier 1 (always) + optional Tier 2 (LLM) allows offline operation while optionally confirming ambiguous cases.

Balances precision (suppress 'Code' as false-positive) and recall (preserve 'Claude Code' compound). Real project/person names are typically multi-word (Alice Chen, Cloud Run) while accidental false positives are single words (Code, Phase), so the bypass aligns the filter with observed reality.

A single syntactic pattern can fire repeatedly on noise (Click, Click, Click), amassing high score. Requiring signals from two different categories enforces orthogonal evidence. Low false-positive rate on closed corpora beats high recall on noisy inputs.

designDecisions.decision: Field Merging (Not Replacement) in Tier 2 LLM
designDecisions.rationale: Tier 1's likely_ai_dialogue and confidence are heuristic ground truth. Tier 2 (LLM) can be wrong on weak models, so it never overrides them; it contributes only persona extraction (fields Tier 1 never computes), with evidence merged via prefixes for audit.

Wikipedia lookup (allow_network=True) is optional, requiring explicit opt-in. Returns 'unknown' locally by default, honoring privacy-by-architecture: no data leaves the machine unless the caller explicitly requests it.

searchDoc.title: Entity System
searchDoc.summary: MemPalace's entity system detects and classifies proper nouns (people, projects, topics) from content using a two-pass signal-based approach: i18n-aware regex extraction with COCA content-word filtering, then contextual signal scoring. A persistent EntityRegistry seeds from onboarding, learns high-confidence candidates, and optionally researches unknowns via Wikipedia. Corpus-origin detection separates AI agent personas from real people before classification.
searchDoc.body: The MemPalace entity system detects and classifies the people, projects, and topics named in your text. Detection runs in two passes. Pass one, extract_candidates, applies language-aware regex patterns loaded from i18n entity sections, matching single-word candidates against per-script character classes (ASCII, Latin with diacritics, Cyrillic, Devanagari) and multi-word candidates through separate phrase patterns. Locale-specific stopwords remove articles and particles. The COCA content-word filter then removes about 600 common English words such as Code, Line, Phase, and Note that appear capitalized but are never entities. Crucially the multi-word path bypasses the COCA filter so compounds like Claude Code survive even though bare Code is suppressed. Only names appearing at least three times advance to scoring. Pass two, score_entity, scores each candidate across six signal types: dialogue markers weighted three times, person verbs weighted two times, pronoun proximity within three lines weighted two times, direct address weighted four times, versioned or hyphenated forms as a project signal weighted three times, and code-file references weighted three times. A guard requires bare colon-prefix dialogue patterns to occur at least twice so metadata lines like Created: 2026-04-21 do not register as speaker tags. Classification by classify_entity enforces the two-signal-category rule: a person needs signals from two distinct categories with a person score of at least five, or a strong pronoun-only signal where pronoun hits are at least five and the pronoun-to-frequency ratio is at least 0.2. This prevents syntactic artifacts like Click, click, click from being read as a person. Before detection, corpus-origin detection determines the platform and any agent-persona names. Tier one is a heuristic counting unambiguous AI brand terms and ambiguous terms under a co-occurrence rule that prevents French novels and astrology forums from false-positiving as AI dialogue. Tier two optionally uses an LLM to extract agent-persona names, which are reclassified out of the people bucket so AI instances never populate family or relationship drawers. The persistent EntityRegistry at ~/.mempalace/entity_registry.json stores three tiers: onboarding, learned, and wiki, with Wikipedia research local-only by default unless network access is explicitly granted, saved via atomic write-then-rename. Detected entities feed closet pointer lines during mining and entity-pair co-occurrence graphs in hallways, keying the entire wing-navigation model and enabling entity-centric search.
